<thought>Based on the observed mass spectrum, the most distinctive isotopic pattern is a relatively strong M+2 peak (≈33 % of the base peak). This magnitude is characteristic of chlorine (35Cl/37Cl) which typically shows an M+2 peak around 25 % of the monoisotopic peak, and the pattern can be amplified by additional carbon‑13 contributions. No other common element (e.g., bromine, sulfur) exhibits an M+2 intensity of this size without accompanying peaks that match their known ratios. Therefore, chlorine is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>['Cl']</final_answer>
